methods.label: Find a lower bound and attain it
methods.explanation:
A resolved debt equals the value of the animals given minus the value of the animals received as change. Both animal values are multiples of 30:
\[
300=30\cdot10,
\qquad 210=30\cdot7.
\]
Because only whole animals are exchanged, the values given and received are each integer multiples of \(\$30\). Their difference must also be a multiple of \(\$30\). Thus no positive debt smaller than \(\$30\) can be resolved.

To show that \(\$30\) itself works, give three goats and receive two pigs as change. The net payment is
\[
3\cdot210-2\cdot300=630-600=30.
\]
This allowed trade attains the lower bound, so the smallest positive debt is \(\boxed{\$30}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The proof uses simple divisibility and an explicit trade, without a general theorem about integer linear combinations.
